citation: Identifying Novel Osteoarthritis-Associated Genes in Human Cartilage Using a Systematic Meta-Analysis and a Multi-Source Integrated Network (PMID: 35457215)
sample_size: 1689 genes analyzed in co-expression network; human osteoarthritic cartilage samples from multiple zones
significance: p < 0.01 for pathway enrichment overlap with cellular senescence drivers
summary: ARPC4-TTLL3 was identified as a novel osteoarthritis-associated protein through systematic meta-analysis of differentially expressed genes in human osteoarthritic cartilage and confirmed by mass spectrometry analysis across different cartilage zones (superficial, middle, and deep) compared to normal controls.

citation: Multiple interactions recruit BLTP2 to ER-PM contacts to control plasma membrane dynamics (PMID: 40899996)
summary: BLTP2/KIAA0100 is a bridge-like lipid transfer protein that mediates bulk lipid transport between the ER and PM by tethering the ER to tubular endosomes and macropinosomes. BLTP2 binds to the PM through interactions with phosphoinositides, adaptor proteins FAM102A/FAM102B, and N-BAR domain proteins. Absence of BLTP2 results in accumulation of intracellular vacuoles connected to the PM, indicating a role in PM dynamics control.

citation: KIAA0100 Modulates Cancer Cell Aggression Behavior of MDA-MB-231 through Microtubule and Heat Shock Proteins (PMID: 29867023)
summary: KIAA0100 silencing by siRNA in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells reduced cell aggregation, reattachment, metastasis, and invasion, and sensitized quiescent cells to anoikis. KIAA0100 stabilizes microtubule structure as a microtubule-binding protein and interacts with heat shock protein HSPA1A to confer anoikis resistance.

citation: Preparation of monoclonal antibody against human KIAA0100 protein and Northern blot analysis of human KIAA0100 gene (PMID: 29404037)
summary: Northern blot analysis in U937 cells revealed that human KIAA0100 gene produces two different mRNA products (6000-10000 bp and 5000-6000 bp), and Western blot showed two protein products (254 kDa and <250 kDa), indicating alternative splicing or post-translational modification.

citation: Bioinformatic prediction and functional characterization of human KIAA0100 gene (PMID: 29404013)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated downregulation of KIAA0100 in U937 cells inhibited cell proliferation and promoted apoptosis. Bioinformatic analysis predicted KIAA0100 localizes to the secretory pathway, contains a signal peptide, transmembrane region, and four FMP27 domains. KIAA0100 is proposed as a novel anti-apoptotic factor in acute monocytic leukemia.

citation: Circ_0000520 interacts with miR-512-5p to upregulate KIAA0100 to promote malignant behaviors in lung cancer (PMID: 35866672)
summary: KIAA0100 is a target of miR-512-5p in lung cancer; the circ_0000520/miR-512-5p/KIAA0100 axis regulates lung cancer cell proliferation, cell cycle progression, migration, invasion, and angiogenesis. KIAA0100 upregulation promotes malignant behaviors in lung cancer cells.

citation: Multiple interactions mediate the localization of BLTP2 at ER-PM contacts to control plasma membrane dynamics (PMID: 39974967)
summary: BLTP2/KIAA0100 localizes at ER-PM contacts through interactions with phosphoinositides, adaptor proteins FAM102A and FAM102B, and N-BAR domain proteins. The protein mediates bulk lipid transport between ER and PM and controls PM dynamics through lipid transfer function.

citation: Identification of BCOX1, a novel gene overexpressed in breast cancer (PMID: 16289875)
summary: BCOX1 (homologous to KIAA0100) is overexpressed in breast carcinoma with mRNA signal localized to the cytoplasm of cancer epithelial cells. BCOX1 mRNA expression is moderately elevated in ductal in situ carcinoma, peaks in invasive and metastatic breast carcinoma, and is absent in benign ductal epithelial cells.

citation: Profiling the Somatic Mutational Landscape of Breast Tumors from Hispanic/Latina Women Reveals Conserved and Unique Characteristics (PMID: 37145128)
summary: Whole-exome and RNA sequencing of 146 breast tumors from Hispanic/Latina women identified a recurrent copy-number amplification at 17q11.2 associated with high KIAA0100 gene expression that has been implicated in breast cancer aggressiveness. This amplification was more prevalent in Hispanic/Latina compared to non-Hispanic White women.

citation: Bioinformatics-based modeling of lung squamous cell carcinoma prognosis and prediction of immunotherapy response (PMID: 39724502)
summary: KIAA0100 was identified as one of 11 key genes in a Cox proportional risk model for predicting lung squamous cell carcinoma patient survival and prognosis. Gene expression variation of KIAA0100 between normal and cancerous lung tissues was significantly associated with patient survival outcomes.

phenotype: increased median lifespan (20%); increased overall lifespan; elevated metabolic rate; preferential use of fat as fuel; dramatically reduced adiposity; increased AMP kinase activity in skeletal muscle; increased β-oxidation in skeletal muscle; increased uncoupling in skeletal muscle; decreased triglyceride content in skeletal muscle; reduced circulating glucose levels; reduced circulating insulin levels; enhanced insulin sensitivity in metabolic tissues; elevated IL-10 in skeletal muscle and serum

citation: Single-cell profiling reveals immune disturbances landscape and HLA-F-mediated immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface in preeclampsia (PMID: 37854606)
summary: HLA-F overexpression in Jar trophoblast cells promoted cell proliferation, invasion, and migration, while underexpression had opposite effects. In NK-92MI cells, HLA-F overexpression increased secretion of immunoregulatory cytokines (CSF1, CCL22) and promoted adaptive NKG2C+ NK cell transformation.

citation: HLA-F regulates the proliferation of trophoblast via PKM2-dependent glycolysis in the pathogenesis of preeclampsia (PMID: 40251569)
summary: HLA-F regulates trophoblast proliferation through PKM2-dependent glycolysis. HLA-F binds the PKM promoter to regulate PKM2 transcription and promotes PKM2 enzyme activity by downregulating lactylation at K305 residue, enhancing glycolytic flux and cell proliferation.

citation: Immunity at maternal-fetal interface: KIR/HLA (Allo)recognition (PMID: 35610960)
summary: HLA-F is a non-classical oligomorphic HLA molecule expressed on trophoblasts at the maternal-fetal interface. It participates in KIR-HLA interactions with decidual NK cells, contributing to immune recognition and tolerance of the semi-allogeneic fetus.

citation: A role for both HLA-F and HLA-G in reproduction and during pregnancy? (PMID: 31558330)
summary: HLA-F can be expressed as open conformers binding multiple KIRs on NK cells, and as peptide-bound HLA-F binding to inhibitory receptors ILT2 and ILT4. HLA-F has potential roles in viral infections, cancer immunology, and fertility/reproduction.

citation: The involvement of HLA-E and -F in pregnancy (PMID: 16487601)
summary: HLA-F is expressed on the surface of extravillous trophoblast that has invaded the maternal decidua, a unique expression site in human development. HLA-F likely contributes collectively with HLA-E and HLA-G to enable fetal development through receptor-ligand interactions.

citation: HLA-F transcriptional and protein differential expression according to its genetic polymorphisms (PMID: 37166140)
summary: HLA-F mRNA is detected in most cell types with protein localized in ER and Golgi apparatus. HLA-F reaches the membrane upon activation of primary cells and cell lines. SNPs rs1362126, rs2523405, and rs2523393 in HLA-F-AS1 region are associated with HLA-F mRNA expression with double-dose effects.

citation: HLA Class Ib-receptor interactions during embryo implantation and early pregnancy (PMID: 35234898)
summary: HLA-F interacts with inhibitory/activating ILT2 and ILT4 receptors and KIRs on uterine NK cells. HLA-F fluctuates during the menstrual cycle with high levels during the implantation window, and its expression correlates with CD56+ NK cell numbers in mid-secretory endometrium.

citation: Tetrameric complexes of HLA-E, HLA-F, and HLA-G (PMID: 12213342)
summary: HLA-F tetrameric complexes bind to ILT2 and ILT4 receptors on immune cells, demonstrating direct receptor-ligand interactions. This methodology enabled identification of HLA-F ligands and functional characterization.

citation: ASHG 2010 - Identification of multiple genetic variants related to nasopharyngeal carcinoma predisposition through genome-wide scan (W. Su, K. Tse, M. Yang, Y. Chang, Y. Shugart)
summary: Two HLA-F SNPs (rs3129055 and rs9258122) showed significant association with nasopharyngeal carcinoma predisposition in a GWAS of 277 NPC patients and 285 controls, with p-values of 7.36×10⁻¹¹ and 3.33×10⁻¹⁰ respectively.

citation: HLA-F and LILRB1 Genetic Polymorphisms Associated with Alloimmunisation in Sickle Cell Disease (PMID: 37686397)
summary: HLA-F genetic polymorphisms in regulatory regions are associated with alloimmunization susceptibility in sickle cell disease patients. HLA-F polymorphisms influence protein expression levels and modulate inflammatory and immune responses through LILRB1 receptor interactions.

citation: Thisse et al. 2022 - The expression of essential selenoproteins during development requires SECIS-binding protein 2-like (PMID: 35210313)

summary: SECISBP2L is a paralogue of SECIS-binding protein 2 (Sbp2) required for selenoprotein synthesis; zebrafish secisbp2l -/- mutants retain full complement of selenoproteins, while sbp2 -/- mutants show selective loss, suggesting SECISBP2L compensates for Sbp2 activity during development.

citation: Xiao et al. 2022 - SECISBP2L-Mediated Selenoprotein Synthesis Is Essential for Autonomous Regulation of Oligodendrocyte Differentiation (PMID: 35760530)

summary: SECISBP2L is highly expressed in differentiating oligodendrocytes and is required for DIO2 (deiodinase 2) translation; conditional knockout of Secisbp2l in oligodendrocyte lineage results in decreased DIO2 and T3 levels, impaired oligodendrocyte differentiation, hypomyelination, and motor deficits, establishing the SECISBP2L-DIO2-T3 pathway in myelin development.

significance: identified through MR analysis with strong causal evidence; significant survival differences
summary: SECISBP2L identified as a tier 1 therapeutic target gene for lung adenocarcinoma with strong causal evidence through Mendelian randomization analysis; included among five genes with most compelling evidence for therapeutic potential based on differential expression, survival analysis, and pathway enrichment.

citation: Biological Functions of the ING Proteins (PMID: 31752342)
summary: ING3 is an epigenetic reader of H3K4Me3 histone mark that targets histone acetyltransferase (HAT) or histone deacetylase (HDAC) complexes to alter chromatin structure. ING3 knockout in mice results in embryonic lethality, indicating essential developmental role.

citation: Loss of Ing3 Expression Results in Growth Retardation and Embryonic Death (PMID: 31905726)
summary: ING3 is a stoichiometric member of the minimal NuA4 histone acetyltransferase (HAT) complex consisting of EAF6, EPC1, ING3, and TIP60. Homozygous Ing3 knockout mice are embryonically lethal with growth retardation and neural tube closure defects, demonstrating ING3 is essential for embryonic development and brain formation.

citation: ING3 protein expression profiling in normal human tissues suggest its role in cellular growth and self-renewal (PMID: 25819753)
summary: ING3 is most highly expressed in small intestine, bone marrow, and epidermis—tissues with rapid cell proliferation and renewal. ING3 expression is significantly higher in proliferating versus quiescent epithelial cells, suggesting ING3 levels may serve as a surrogate for growth rate.

citation: ING3 inhibits the malignant progression of lung adenocarcinoma by negatively regulating ITGB4 expression to inactivate Src/FAK signaling (PMID: 38281617)
sample_size: NCI-H1975 cells and nude mice xenograft model
summary: ING3 negatively regulates integrin β4 (ITGB4) expression to inactivate Src/focal adhesion kinase (FAK) signaling in lung adenocarcinoma. ING3 overexpression restrains proliferation, migration, invasion and induces cell cycle arrest, with effects reversed by ITGB4 overexpression.

citation: The tumor suppressor ING3 is degraded by SCF(Skp2)-mediated ubiquitin-proteasome system (PMID: 19935701)
summary: ING3 undergoes degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway via interaction with the SCF(Skp2) E3 ligase complex. Lysine 96 is essential for ING3 ubiquitination; Skp2 knockdown stabilizes ING3 and enhances its tumor-suppressive functions including G1 cell-cycle arrest and UV-induced apoptosis.

citation: ING3 promotes prostate cancer growth by activating the androgen receptor (PMID: 28511652)
sample_size: 265 prostate cancer biopsies; LNCaP and C4-2 cell lines; TCGA n=498; tissue microarray n=256
summary: ING3 activates the androgen receptor (AR) by serving as a scaffold to increase interaction between TIP60 and AR in the cytoplasm, enhancing receptor acetylation and nuclear translocation. This chromatin-independent cytoplasmic activity promotes androgen-regulated gene expression and prostate cancer growth.

citation: Overexpression of ING3 is associated with attenuation of migration and invasion in breast cancer (PMID: 34007308)
summary: ING3 overexpression significantly inhibits migratory and invasive abilities of MCF7 and HCC1937 breast cancer cells. ING3 expression is lower in cancer tissues compared to normal tissues, with lower expression predicting poor prognosis in luminal A and HER2-enriched breast cancer subtypes.

citation: Prognostic significance of nuclear ING3 expression in human cutaneous melanoma (PMID: 17634537)
sample_size: 58 dysplastic nevi, 114 primary melanomas, 50 metastatic melanomas
summary: Nuclear ING3 expression is remarkably reduced in malignant melanomas compared with dysplastic nevi. Reduced nuclear ING3 expression correlates with poorer disease-specific 5-year survival and is an independent prognostic factor; survival rates drop from 93% (strong nuclear staining) to 44% (negative-to-moderate staining) in high-risk melanomas.

citation: Human ex vivo prostate tissue model system identifies ING3 as an oncoprotein (PMID: 29381681)
sample_size: Ex vivo prostate tissues; tissue microarray; multiple cancer cell lines
summary: ING3 stimulates cellular proliferation in ex vivo benign prostate hyperplasia tissues and transforms normal human dermal fibroblasts. ING3 is required for proliferation of breast, ovarian, and prostate cancer cells. ING3 controls cell cycle gene expression by associating with chromatin modifiers and the H3K4me3 mark at transcriptional start sites.

summary: MAP4K4 is activated by RAP2 GTPase in response to low ECM stiffness and stimulates LATS1/2 kinases to inhibit YAP and TAZ, thereby integrating mechanical signals into the Hippo tumor suppressor pathway.

citation: MAP4K4 exacerbates cardiac microvascular injury in diabetes by facilitating S-nitrosylation modification of Drp1 (PMID: 38724987)

citation: MAP4K4 aggravates microvascular anomalies in diabetic retinopathy in a YTHDF2-dependent manner (PMID: 40072537)

citation: MAP4K4 and cancer: ready for the main stage? (PMID: 37223681)
summary: MAP4K4 is a serine/threonine kinase that activates pro-proliferative pathways (JNK and MLK3), promotes tumor cell proliferation and invasion, and alters cytoskeleton/actin function. MAP4K4 knockout is embryonic lethal due to impaired somite development.

citation: The molecular basis of the dichotomous functionality of MAP4K4 in proliferation and cell motility control in cancer (PMID: 36568222)
summary: MAP4K4 functions as an upstream integrator of extracellular cues with dual roles: activating JNK signaling for proliferation while also activating the Hippo tumor suppressor pathway, creating a dichotomous pro-metastatic and growth-suppressive functionality.

citation: Cooperation of Striatin 3 and MAP4K4 promotes growth and tissue invasion (PMID: 35941177)

citation: MAP4K4 expression in cardiomyocytes: multiple isoforms, multiple phosphorylations and interactions with striatins (PMID: 34032269)

citation: MAP4K4 regulates forces at cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesions to promote collective cell migration (PMID: 37369604)

citation: NUP85 alleviates lipid metabolism and inflammation by regulating PI3K/AKT signaling pathway in nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (PMID: 38617542)
summary: NUP85 regulates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway and interacts with CCR2 to modulate lipid metabolism and inflammation in NAFLD. NUP85 knockdown decreased fat disorder and inflammation levels in MCD-induced mice and FFA-stimulated AML-12 cells, while ISRIB (NUP85 inhibitor) alleviated NAFLD.

citation: NUP85 siRNA loaded red blood cell-derived extracellular vesicles alleviate hepatic steatosis in MASLD (PMID: 41413582)
summary: NUP85 promotes lipid accumulation in hepatocytes via the SLC27A1/PPAR-γ signaling pathway. Serum NUP85 levels are significantly elevated in MASLD patients and correlate with disease severity. RBC-EVs@siNUP85 delivery system effectively silenced NUP85 in hepatocytes, alleviating hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress in both in vitro and in vivo models.

citation: NUP85 as a Neurodevelopmental Gene: From Podocyte to Neuron (PMID: 38136965)
summary: Compound heterozygous NUP85 variants (c.611T>A, p.Val204Glu and c.1904T>G, p.Leu635Arg) cause steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome with severe neurodevelopmental impairment including microcephaly, axial hypotonia, seizures, corpus callosum hypoplasia, and simplified cerebral cortex gyration, expanding NUP85's role beyond renal function to brain development.

citation: Nucleoporin-associated steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (PMID: 39331077)
summary: NUP85 mutations cause autosomal recessive steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome with median onset at 7 years and progression to kidney failure at median age 8.5 years. Kidney biopsies reveal focal segmental glomerulosclerosis in 89% of patients. Extrarenal manifestations include neurological, growth/development, cardiovascular disorders, and congenital malformations.

citation: Docking a flexible basket onto the core of the nuclear pore complex (PMID: 39138317)
summary: NUP85 is a subunit of the Y-complex of the nuclear pore complex that interacts with basket subunit Nup60 through a tripartite junction involving short linear motifs. This interaction couples transcription to mRNA quality control and export, and was validated through AlphaFold-based screens, electron microscopy, membrane-templated reconstitution, and in vivo validation.

citation: An Arabidopsis Nucleoporin NUP85 modulates plant responses to ABA and salt stress (PMID: 29232718)
summary: Arabidopsis NUP85 mutants exhibit reduced expression of stress-responsive genes (RD29A, COR15A, COR47) in response to ABA and salt stress. NUP85 associates with HOS1 and other nucleoporins within the nup107-160 complex and directly interacts with mediator subunit MED18, linking the nuclear pore complex to mediator complex in stress gene regulation.

citation: Analysis of correlation between high expression of nucleoporin 85 (NUP85) and immune cell infiltration in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 38952090)
summary: NUP85 mRNA and protein are upregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma across different stages and grades, with 19% mutation rate significantly affecting overall survival, disease-specific survival, and progression-free survival. NUP85 is highly expressed in macrophages, B cells, and T cells and positively correlates with immune cell infiltration. GO/KEGG enrichment shows NUP85 co-expressed genes are enriched in cell cycle and chromosome segregation pathways.

citation: Deficient chaperone-mediated autophagy in macrophage aggravates inflammation of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis by targeting Nup85 (PMID: 36912786)
summary: Nup85 functions as a substrate for chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA) in macrophages. CMA dysfunction in hepatic macrophages impairs Nup85 degradation, aggravating monocyte recruitment and promoting liver inflammation and fibrosis in NASH. Inhibition of Nup85 attenuated steatosis and monocyte recruitment caused by CMA deficiency in NASH mice.

citation: Case report: Compound heterozygous NUP85 variants cause autosomal recessive primary microcephaly (PMID: 36846113)
sample_size: 1 index patient plus 1 additional unrelated individual
summary: Compound heterozygous NUP85 variants cause primary autosomal recessive microcephaly without steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome or Seckel syndrome, expanding the phenotypic spectrum. Patient-derived fibroblasts showed reduced cell viability, and structural simulation predicted the variants alter NUP85 structure and interactions with neighboring nucleoporins.

citation: Nucleoporin 85 interacts with influenza A virus PB1 and PB2 to promote its replication by facilitating nuclear import of ribonucleoprotein (PMID: 36051755)
summary: NUP85 interacts with influenza A virus polymerase subunits PB1 and PB2 in an RNA-dependent manner to facilitate nuclear import of viral ribonucleoprotein. NUP85 knockdown delayed vRNP nuclear import and suppressed viral replication. NUP85 assists binding of PB1 to RanBP5 and PB2 to importin α1/α7, and NUP85 expression is downregulated upon IAV infection.

citation: NUP85 Mediates Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress through the USP47/ASK1 Signaling Pathway to Regulate the Progression of Liver Fibrosis (PMID: 41903125)
summary: NUP85 is elevated in liver fibrosis and regulates the USP47/ASK1 signaling pathway. NUP85 competitively binds USP47 to deubiquitinate ASK1 at lysine 805, exacerbating endoplasmic reticulum stress and collagen deposition. NUP85 knockdown ameliorated liver injury and fibrosis, while overexpression promoted pathological changes. CREKA-coupled liposomes delivered Mogroside V (NUP85 inhibitor) to attenuate fibrosis.

citation: Inactivating Mutations of the IK Gene Weaken Ku80/Ku70-Mediated DNA Repair and Sensitize Endometrial Cancer to Chemotherapy (PMID: 34065218)
significance: Patients with IK-inactivating mutations had significantly better overall survival (10-year follow-up)
summary: IK interacts with Ku80 and Ku70 proteins to mediate DNA repair. Co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry identified these protein interactions. IK knockdown led to inactivation of Ku80/Ku70-mediated DNA repair signaling and sensitization to cisplatin treatment in endometrial cancer cells.

citation: Implication of a new molecule IK in CD34+ hematopoietic progenitor cell proliferation and differentiation (PMID: 9160666)
sample_size: CD34+ cells from human umbilical cord blood
significance: 70% decrease in colony size with IK antisense inhibition compared to controls
summary: IK gene transcripts are expressed in CD34+ hematopoietic progenitor cells from human umbilical cord blood. IK expression inversely correlates with HLA-DR expression during growth factor-induced CD34+ cell proliferation and differentiation. IK antisense oligodeoxynucleotide inhibition decreased colony formation by 70% in multilineage early erythroid and granulomonocytic progenitors.

citation: Ikaros is expressed in developing striatal neurons and involved in enkephalinergic differentiation (PMID: 17504264)
sample_size: Developing striatal tissue and neuronal cultures
significance: Mutant animals lacking DNA-binding domain of Ik had deficit in ENK mRNA+ cells; animals lacking protein interaction domain showed no deficit
summary: Ikaros (Ik) isoforms Ik-1 and Ik-2 are specifically expressed in embryonic striatum and bind Ik-like cis-regulatory DNA elements on the enkephalin (ENK) gene. Ik proteins are expressed by both proliferating (BrdU+/nestin+) and post-mitotic differentiating (MAP2+) cells between embryonic day 12 and post-natal day 2. Ik acts as a positive regulator of ENK gene expression through its DNA-binding domain.

citation: Expression of the Ikaros gene family in childhood acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (PMID: 12028018)
significance: Ik6 expression in childhood precursor B-ALL: 26.3% vs. absent in other types (p=0.0001); inverse correlation with Ai1 (p=0.005) and He1 (p=0.035)
summary: Ikaros (Ik) gene family expression analyzed in 97 ALL cases (64 childhood, 33 infant). Ik expression detected in all cases; dominant negative isoform Ik6 expressed in 10/38 (26.3%) childhood precursor B-ALL cases but absent in other childhood ALL types. Expression of Ik6 was inversely correlated with Aiolos (Ai1) and Helios (He1) expression.

citation: A new cytokine (IK) down-regulating HLA class II: monoclonal antibodies, cloning and chromosome localization (PMID: 7970704)
significance: IK factor almost completely abolishes HLA class II expression induced by Cycloheximide in Colo 205 cells
summary: IK is a 19 kDa cytokine secreted by leukemic K562 cells and cancer cells that inhibits HLA Class II antigen induction by IFN-gamma. IK gene maps to chromosome 2p15-p14 and encodes a 2.1 kb mRNA with no homology to known cytokines. Transient transfection of IK cDNA in COS cells induces secretion of biologically active 19 kDa protein.

citation: Forced expression of the Ikaros 6 isoform in human placental blood CD34(+) cells impairs their ability to differentiate toward the B-lymphoid lineage (PMID: 11675337)
significance: Ik6 expression impaired B-lymphoid differentiation in both in vitro and in vivo assays
summary: Forced expression of Ikaros 6 (Ik6), a dominant negative isoform lacking the DNA-binding domain, in human cord blood CD34+ progenitors reduces their capacity to produce B lymphoid cells. This was demonstrated in two independent assays: in vitro coculture with MS-5 stromal cells and xenotransplantation in NOD-SCID mice. Results suggest the balance between Ikaros isoforms is critical for hematopoietic differentiation.

citation: ASHG 2012 - Frequency of non-DNA-binding Ikaros isoforms in childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia and relapse or death risk
sample_size: 76 children with newly diagnosed ALL (69 B-ALL, 7 T-ALL)
significance: Non-functional Ikaros isoforms (Ik-6/Ik-8) associated with relapse and death in ALL children
summary: Non-DNA-binding Ikaros isoforms Ik-6 and Ik-8 detected in 18/69 (26.1%) B-ALL cases. Fourteen B-ALL patients expressed Ik-6, 3 presented Ik-8, and 1 showed Ik-8 variant. Seven patients with non-functional isoforms developed adverse events (3 relapses, 4 deaths); notably, 5 of 7 had standard risk by conventional prognostic factors at diagnosis.

citation: ASHG 2009 - Akt-dependent regulation of potassium channels by IGF-1 in cardiomyocytes
sample_size: Freshly isolated neonatal rat ventricular myocytes
significance: IGF-1 effect on IK completely reversed by dominant-negative Akt (Ad.Akt179M); PI3K inhibitor LY294002 abrogated all effects
summary: The delayed outward rectifier current (IK), the major ion channel responsible for ventricular repolarization, is negatively regulated by IGF-1 through the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes. IGF-1 reduced IK functional density from 4.1±0.5 to 2.6±0.3 pA/pF; this effect was eliminated by PI3K inhibitor LY294002 and mimicked by constitutively activated PI3K or wild-type Akt.
